text: When a KdV soliton (v, amplitude 1.5, starting at x=-8) moving rightward encounters a smoothed Burgers bore (u, u_L=1.5, u_R=0, centered at x=0) in the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV PDE, does the soliton transmit, reflect, fuse, or get destroyed? Does a recognizable v-peak survive with amplitude >= 0.5 at T=8?

method: Fourier pseudospectral, conservative form fluxes, explicit RK4, no dealiasing
bank_use_rationale: No knowledge bank provided. E1 is simplest meaningful baseline: pseudospectral handles v_xxx cleanly on periodic domain; explicit RK4 is the standard baseline time integrator; conservative flux form used to minimize spurious growth.

diagnostics.failure_mode: u blows up first; v still reasonable => aliasing in (3/2)u^2 Burgers nonlinearity, not dispersive stiffness

rationale: Blow-up at t~1.04 due to aliasing from Burgers nonlinearity steepening the bore. u reaches ±228, far exceeding the |u_max|<5 criterion. Single-component fix: add 2/3-rule dealiasing to suppress aliasing in all nonlinear product terms.

F1 shows u blow-up from aliasing in pseudospectral nonlinear terms. Add 2/3-rule (Orszag) dealiasing as the single-component upgrade for E2; keep all other components (RK4, dt=1e-4, pseudospectral, conservative form) identical.

method: Fourier pseudospectral + explicit RK4 + 2/3-rule (Orszag) dealiasing on all nonlinear products; otherwise identical to E1
bank_use_rationale: No bank available. F1 showed aliasing blow-up in u; 2/3-rule dealiasing is the standard single-component fix for pseudospectral Burgers aliasing. All other components unchanged from E1.

diagnostics.soliton_behavior: transmitted rightward through bore: x=-8 to x=13.83, amplitude reduced from 1.50 to 0.66 but survived

rationale: All phenomenon targets met: v_peak=0.665>=0.5, |u|_max=3.45<5, bore stable. v-mass conserved exactly (3.0000 all snapshots). Soliton transmitted through bore with amplitude reduction but survival. Stopping early.
E2 with 2/3-rule dealiasing produced a successful simulation: soliton transmitted through bore, both phenomenon criteria satisfied, v-mass conserved. No further iterations needed.
